ENTITY_PROPERTIES_SCHEMA.description: Entity fields to persist. Must include title and status. If created_at, updated_at, or source are omitted, server fills defaults.

title.description: Required short title. Example: 'Protect account settings endpoint'.

status.description: Required lifecycle state. Allowed values depend on entity type; backward-compatible legacy statuses are also accepted. Examples: 'open', 'passing', 'accepted', 'active'.

source.description: Optional provenance string. Example: '.kb/requirements/REQ-cli-gc.md'. Defaults to 'mcp://kibi/upsert'.

kind.description: Who authored the entity: human, agent, migration (backfilled by kibi migrate) or import.

ref.description: Source reference for the authored content: URL, document path, ticket, commit or conversation id.

approved_by.description: The person who reviewed and approved this entity's content. Distinct from the requirement-level approved_by of an exception.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 time the provenance was recorded.

origin.description: Optional provenance: who authored the entity (kind: human, agent, migration, import) and on what authority (ref, approved_by, recorded_at). Omit it to keep an existing entity's origin; a new entity written without one is recorded as {kind: agent, recorded_at: <write time>}. A supplied origin without recorded_at gets the write time.

semantic_text.description: Requirement-only authored prose used for semantic inventory hashes and UTF-8 spans. Keep text_ref available for independent document or code evidence.

logic_claims.description: Requirement-only manifest of every atomic normative claim key returned by kb_model mode analyze (CLI: kibi model). A requirement is logic-complete only when every key is grounded by a linked property_value or predicate fact with the same claim_key.

semantic_clauses.description: Optional complete atomic decomposition used by kb_model mode analyze and proposition-complete ingestion. Preserve it when automatic sentence splitting needs a reviewed override.

semantic_inventory_version.description: Requirement-only proposition ledger contract version returned by kb_model mode analyze (CLI: kibi model).

semantic_source_field.description: Requirement field whose exact UTF-8 bytes anchor semantic_inventory spans.

approved_by.description: Requirement-only. The human who approved this exception requirement. An exception that exempts a requirement and is specified_by a success scenario makes that scenario feasible only when approved_by is set.

approval_ref.description: Requirement-only. Optional reference to the exception's approval decision record.

failure_side_waiver.description: Requirement-only. Why the requirement has no failure side to test (its claims state a capability or output shape). Waives happy_path_only once failure_side_waiver_approved_by is set.

failure_side_waiver_approved_by.description: Requirement-only. The person who accepted failure_side_waiver.

firmness.description: req/adr only. firm = a human stated it as a rule (needs origin.ref to their words); its title, meaning or firmness changes only with new human words (a new origin.ref) or by supersede. default = delegated or agent choice; exploratory = flagged guess. Absent = default if an agent wrote it, else firm.

required_evidence.description: Requirement-only. Weakest evidence level it accepts; the evidence-floor rule fails below it. Absent = tested if firm, else unverified.

rationale.description: Requirement-only. Why the requirement exists, in one or two sentences from whoever stated the intent; not part of the checked meaning.

exempts_claims.description: Requirement-only. Claim keys of the exempted requirement whose constraints this exception waives; omit to waive the whole requirement.

semantic_source_hash.description: SHA-256 of the exact semantic source text returned in the advisor inventory contract.

sourceFile.description: Optional code source file for symbol entities. Example: 'src/auth/login.ts'.

granularity_reason.description: Optional justification for a coarse file/module-level symbol traceability relationship when narrower function/class/type symbols exist.

symbol_role.description: Optional role classification for symbol entities. Example: 'behavioral'.

verification_scope.description: Optional typed verification scope for test entities. Example: 'end_to_end'.

verification_perspective.description: Optional typed verification perspective for test entities. Example: 'consumer'.

proof_contract.description: Semantic proof contract binding this test to explicit proof obligations executed by one configured integration.

kind.description: What the checker establishes; absent means e2e. exhaustive, typecheck, arithmetic, smt, rule, state_machine and regex must leave a kibi.code-certificate.v1 that Kibi re-checks before the receipt counts as proved. source reads the contract's source itself: the run may leave {version, kind: source, test_id, source} or nothing, and Kibi stores its own read as the certificate.

source.description: source: the project source a source proof reads. A project source Kibi reads by itself. reader json or yaml: {file, path?, select?: keys|values|items}. glob: {pattern, capture?, ignore?} (capture true reads what each * matched). openapi: {file, select?: operations|unsecured_operations|security_schemes|responses}. references: {files, extract: env|imports|calls|string_args|thrown|property, callee?, key?, ignore?} over TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and SWI-Prolog files. schema: {format: drizzle|prisma|sql, file (drizzle, prisma) or files (sql migrations), exports?, table?, select?: tables|columns|required_columns|nullable_columns|foreign_keys}. routes: {file, export, framework?: hono|express, path_prefix?, names_from?, select?: routes|middleware}. validator: {file, export, select?: fields|required_fields|optional_fields}. prolog: {file, functor: Name/Arity, arg?} reads one argument of every fact with that functor in a SWI-Prolog file (requires/1 in pack.pl), without running it. Paths are repository-relative. A member Kibi cannot read statically fails the read with its location.

domain_source.description: exhaustive and typecheck: the symbol that defines the finite domain (typecheck: also the type whose fields a required_fields fact names). state_machine: the transition table or next-state function. The proof must import it from its source file; a hand-listed domain downgrades the receipt to example. Kibi reads the export named `export`, or the symbol's title when `export` is absent.

export.description: The name the domain is exported under in the symbol's source file, when the symbol's title is not that name.

field.description: exhaustive: when the export is a list of records, the field of each record that names a domain member (a catalog's name).

arg.description: A SWI-Prolog predicate's argument (1-based) whose solutions Kibi reads, when the predicate takes more than one argument (operator/2 with arg 1 lists each operator's name).

witness.description: typecheck: the repository-relative witness file Kibi compiles (an exhaustive switch ending in never, or a mapped type over the domain).

proves.description: Certificate kinds: the requirement claim keys (CLAIM-...) this certificate proves. Each must be a modeled claim of a current requirement the test reaches through its scenarios. Kibi derives what the certificate must establish from the claim's grounding fact (a set fact for exhaustive or typecheck, a numeric fact for arithmetic or smt, a rule, predicate or set fact for rule and state_machine, a string fact for regex); a claim with no such derivation is only attested and never counts as proved.

value_source.description: arithmetic and smt: code constants the assumptions read. Kibi evaluates each export at ingest and requires the certificate to assume the variable equals that value, so the proof is about the code and not only the knowledge base. With measure count the value is the size of a list, set, map or object export, so a count claim reads the collection itself. A dotted export (POLICY.eventLimit) reads one field of an object export. An entry {source, measure: count} counts the members Kibi reads from a project source (routes, tables, environment variables).

arg.description: A SWI-Prolog predicate's argument (1-based) whose solutions Kibi reads, when the predicate takes more than one argument (operator/2 with arg 1 lists each operator's name).

source.description: A project source Kibi reads by itself. reader json or yaml: {file, path?, select?: keys|values|items}. glob: {pattern, capture?, ignore?} (capture true reads what each * matched). openapi: {file, select?: operations|unsecured_operations|security_schemes|responses}. references: {files, extract: env|imports|calls|string_args|thrown|property, callee?, key?, ignore?} over TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and SWI-Prolog files. schema: {format: drizzle|prisma|sql, file (drizzle, prisma) or files (sql migrations), exports?, table?, select?: tables|columns|required_columns|nullable_columns|foreign_keys}. routes: {file, export, framework?: hono|express, path_prefix?, names_from?, select?: routes|middleware}. validator: {file, export, select?: fields|required_fields|optional_fields}. prolog: {file, functor: Name/Arity, arg?} reads one argument of every fact with that functor in a SWI-Prolog file (requires/1 in pack.pl), without running it. Paths are repository-relative. A member Kibi cannot read statically fails the read with its location.

measure.description: value (default for an export): the export is a number. count (the only measure of a source): the number of members of a list, set, map or object export, or of a source.

predicate_source.description: rule: the code function behind each predicate a claim's rule, predicate or set fact names, keyed by predicate name. Each export takes the predicate's arguments in order and returns a boolean; Kibi calls it on every combination of its argument domains.

export.description: The exported function's name in the symbol's source file. Without it Kibi reads the export named by the symbol's title.

harness_for.description: The predicate is a test harness that decides the predicate by driving these code symbols (for example by calling the handler with each role). The symbols must be covered_by the test; a claim the harness proves is bound with scope harness.

domains.description: rule: the finite domain of each argument type, keyed by type name (an array, Set, Map or object export, or a Python list, set, dict or Enum), or {source} for the members Kibi reads from a project source (every route, every table, every environment variable). state_machine with a next-state function: the `state` and `event` domains it is called on.

arg.description: A SWI-Prolog predicate's argument (1-based) whose solutions Kibi reads, when the predicate takes more than one argument (operator/2 with arg 1 lists each operator's name).

source.description: A project source Kibi reads by itself. reader json or yaml: {file, path?, select?: keys|values|items}. glob: {pattern, capture?, ignore?} (capture true reads what each * matched). openapi: {file, select?: operations|unsecured_operations|security_schemes|responses}. references: {files, extract: env|imports|calls|string_args|thrown|property, callee?, key?, ignore?} over TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and SWI-Prolog files. schema: {format: drizzle|prisma|sql, file (drizzle, prisma) or files (sql migrations), exports?, table?, select?: tables|columns|required_columns|nullable_columns|foreign_keys}. routes: {file, export, framework?: hono|express, path_prefix?, names_from?, select?: routes|middleware}. validator: {file, export, select?: fields|required_fields|optional_fields}. prolog: {file, functor: Name/Arity, arg?} reads one argument of every fact with that functor in a SWI-Prolog file (requires/1 in pack.pl), without running it. Paths are repository-relative. A member Kibi cannot read statically fails the read with its location.

arg.description: A SWI-Prolog predicate's argument (1-based) whose solutions Kibi reads, when the predicate takes more than one argument (operator/2 with arg 1 lists each operator's name).

initial_source.description: state_machine: the export holding the initial state (or states), needed for initial_states and reachable_states facts.

arg.description: A SWI-Prolog predicate's argument (1-based) whose solutions Kibi reads, when the predicate takes more than one argument (operator/2 with arg 1 lists each operator's name).

pattern_source.description: regex: the export holding the code's pattern (a RegExp, or a Python re.Pattern) or string constant that a string fact is about.

constraint_source.description: arithmetic and smt: the typed numeric property_value facts the certificate's assumptions come from. Kibi checks the assumptions (or the query's assertions) are exactly these facts' constraints, so the proof is about the knowledge base, not numbers the test chose.

proof_bindings.description: Optional native-runner bindings (native ids, aliases, source coordinates) for proof obligations. Bindings are provenance metadata and never replace the semantic contract.

items.description: Kibi-derived kibi.proof-receipt.v2 (kibi.proof-receipt.v1 entries are still read). Receipts are never caller-authored; kb_ingest_proof derives them from kibi.proof-run.v1 artifacts.

claim_bindings.description: Certificate kinds: how the certificate binds to each claim its contract names in proves, judged at ingest. derived means Kibi derived the certificate's obligation from the claim's grounding fact and the certificate satisfies it; attested means no derivation exists and the author vouches for it (never proved); rejected names why.

proof_receipts.description: Append-only proof evidence. Proof accepts only the newest valid passed receipt bound to the current code snapshot, current contract hash, and effective execution fingerprint within the seven-day freshness window. Ingest rotates the oldest entries at the cap.

fact_kind.description: Optional fact lane kind for fact entities. Strict lane uses 'subject' and 'property_value'; context lane uses 'observation' or 'meta'; ontology lane uses 'predicate_schema' or 'predicate'. Use kb_model (mode requirement or predicates) when starting from prose.

subject_key.description: Snake_case only. Optional canonical subject key for strict fact entities. Example: 'user.session'. Do not use subjectKey in kb_upsert.properties.

property_key.description: Snake_case only. Optional canonical property key for property_value facts. Example: 'session.timeout_minutes'. Do not use propertyKey in kb_upsert.properties.

operator.description: Optional comparison operator for property_value facts. Example: 'eq'. 'matches' (string facts only): value_string is a JavaScript regular expression (u flag) every value must match as a whole. Set facts only: 'includes' means every member of value_set has the property and other members may have it too; 'subset_of' means every member that has the property is in value_set ('every env var the server reads is one of ...'); 'excludes' means no member of value_set has it ('never imports md5'); 'eq' on a set means exactly those members.

value_type.description: Optional typed value discriminator for property_value facts. Pair with exactly one value_string, value_int, value_number, value_bool, or value_set (set: a list of members, with operator eq, includes, subset_of or excludes); do not use generic value.

value_string.description: Optional string value for property_value facts.

value_int.description: Optional integer value for property_value facts.

value_number.description: Optional number value for property_value facts.

value_bool.description: Optional boolean value for property_value facts.

value_set.description: Optional exact set of values for property_value facts with value_type set, such as the members a domain must have.

unit.description: Optional unit for numeric property_value facts.

scope.description: Optional scope qualifier for fact entities.

polarity.description: Optional polarity for property_value or predicate facts.

closed_world.description: Optional closed-world marker for strict fact interpretation.

canonical_key.description: Optional canonical identity key for predicate or strict fact claims.

claim_key.description: Stable key of the atomic prose clause grounded by this fact, derived from claim_text. Optional: when omitted, Kibi derives it; when sent, it must equal the derived key.

claim_text.description: Exact atomic requirement clause represented by this fact, retained for human audit. On a grounding fact Kibi derives claim_key from it; an observation or meta fact quotes the clause it is about without a key.

dimension_waiver.description: Fact-only. Why the quantifier word in claim_text ranges over nothing, so the claim needs no count, set or rule. Waives dimension_unrepresented once dimension_waiver_approved_by is set.

dimension_waiver_approved_by.description: Fact-only. The person who accepted dimension_waiver.

case_waiver.description: Fact-only. Why the edge cases derived from this fact are covered some other way or cannot occur. Waives uncovered_case once case_waiver_approved_by is set.

case_waiver_approved_by.description: Fact-only. The person who accepted case_waiver.

predicate_name.description: Optional predicate name for ontology predicate facts. Prefer kb_model mode predicates before hand-writing predicate_name.

predicate_args.description: Optional ordered predicate arguments for ontology predicate facts. Prefer kb_model mode predicates before hand-writing predicate_args.

predicate_namespace.description: Optional namespace for a project-local predicate schema.

argument_names.description: Ordered argument role names for predicate_schema facts.

argument_types.description: Ordered argument types for predicate_schema facts.

key_arguments.description: predicate_schema only: argument names that determine the remaining arguments (a functional dependency), e.g. ["sensor"] for reading(sensor, value). Rule contradiction analysis treats two atoms with identical keys as the same fact; without it the predicate is multivalued and opposing rules stay unresolved instead of disjoint.

argument_constants.description: predicate_schema only: allowed constants keyed by argument name, e.g. {"severity": ["warning", "info"]}. Predicate facts must use a listed constant for those arguments; unlisted arguments stay open.

argument_aliases.description: predicate_schema only: legacy spellings keyed by argument name, each mapped to a declared constant, e.g. {"severity": {"warn": "warning"}}. kibi migrate rewrites facts that still use an alias.

aliases.description: Optional vocabulary aliases for predicate discovery.

examples.description: Optional ground-term examples for a predicate schema.

part_of.description: subject only: defined subject keys this subject is a part of. A dotted key prefix that is itself a defined subject is broader already.

kind_of.description: subject only: defined subject keys this subject is a kind of (a read-only review is a kind of review view).

distinct_from.description: subject only: similar defined subject keys this subject was checked to differ from; the body says how. Silences subject-duplicate for those pairs.

semantic_inventory.description: Requirement proposition ledger returned by kb_model mode analyze (CLI: kibi model); preserve entries while modeling each assertive span. An unmodeled normative, condition, exception or definition entry must carry `subjects`: the defined subject keys it is about.

pair_reviews.description: Requirement only: verdicts on stored pairs (a relates_to edge or a shared subject) whose unmodeled claims cannot be modeled. Each entry: with (the other requirement, which a relates_to edge must link), verdict (no_conflict with separated_by naming the condition or term that separates them; interacts with resolved_by naming a current scenario, fact, requirement or claim_key that resolves it; conflict, which stays blocking until a person decides), claims (claim_key and payload_hash of each unmodeled claim of both requirements) and origin (kind human or agent; an agent's verdict on a must or firm requirement counts only with approved_by from a person). Model the claims first; a verdict is the fallback.

rule_ir.description: Schema-validated kibi.logic.v1 rule IR. It is persisted as data and never executed as caller-supplied Prolog.

rule_schema_id.description: Rule schema fact ID used to validate this rule.

semantic_key.description: Canonical semantic identity of the normalized logical model.

RELATIONSHIPS_SCHEMA.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call. For requirement encoding, prefer `constrains` + `requires_property` for strict property facts or `requires_predicate` for ontology predicate facts. Side effect: asserts edges in KB.

type.description: Relationship type enum. Use only supported values. Direction semantics follow KB model (e.g., implements symbol->req, verified_by req/scenario->test, executable_for symbol->test).
